history.summary: An ancient east-facing Vishnu temple in a forested valley beneath the Brahmagiri range, near the Karnataka border. Legend: Lord Brahma, travelling on a swan, descended at the spot, found a Vishnu idol under an Amla (nelli) tree, and installed it with the devas - hence Sahyamalaka ('Malaka of the Sahya') and Thirunelli (holy gooseberry). At Brahma's request Vishnu blessed the local waters with sin-washing power, creating the Papanashini stream; drops of amrit from Garuda's pot are also said to have fallen in. Parasurama is believed to have performed his father Jamadagni's last rites here. The temple is a major balitharpanam (ancestral rite) centre; Panchatheertham pond has a Vishnu footprint stone. Dating conflicts: casualwalker.com cites Bhaskara Ravi Varma (962-1019 CE); others claim 1500 or 3000 years. The CSV 'state' column wrongly holds 'Wayanad' (the district); actual town is Thirunelli, state Kerala. Morning hours sourced (5:30 AM-12 noon, wayanad.com); evening session not verified - verify.

name: Thirunelli Temple
town_description: Thirunelli is a forest village in north Wayanad, Kerala, at about 900 m in the Brahmagiri range near the Karnataka border, roughly 32 km from Mananthavady. A pilgrimage and nature-tourism hub, it draws devotees for ancestral rites at the Papanashini and trekkers for Brahmagiri and nearby Pakshipathalam.

travel.railway: Nearest major stations at Kozhikode/Thalassery (verify); then road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Karkidaka Vavu (Jul-Aug) for balitharpanam ancestral rites
